transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Lee. It's so nice to meet you, and thank you for fitting me in. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because I might have gotten just a little... over-enthusiastic lately? I volunteer with the local historical society, and I sort of took on our big fundraiser project. I just really wanted to help out, you know? But I suppose I acted like I could run the whole thing completely by myself. 

I was starting all these new quilt designs, calling volunteers, making all these elaborate schedules... and I ended up promising deadlines that, looking back, I couldn't possibly meet. I really didn't mean to step on any toes or cause a fuss, I just wanted it to be wonderful for everyone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this okay.
Over this same period, have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual, yet still feel full of energy the next day?

Well, um... yes, I suppose for a little while there I was only sleeping a few hours a night. But I honestly felt wonderful! I'd wake up bright and early, just completely ready to sew or make my phone calls. I just had so much I wanted to do for the society, you know? 

But... lately, things have changed a bit. I feel a little embarrassed admitting this, because I really should have a better handle on my schedule, but now I seem to either just lie awake at night worrying about everything, or I end up sleeping in quite late and somehow still feel completely worn out. I probably just pushed myself a little too hard and tired myself out, don't you think? Am I giving you the right kind of information?
During that period when you felt full of energy and needed little sleep, about how many days in a row did that last?

Oh, dear... I'm really not sure exactly. I feel a little silly admitting this, but I wasn't really keeping track. I was just so focused on getting everything perfect for the society, you know? 

It just felt like a... a nice little stretch of time where I was getting so much done. I'd hate to give you the wrong answer, so I'd rather not guess and steer you wrong. I just know it went on for a little while before I started feeling so worn down. I'm so sorry I don't have a specific number for you... is it okay if I'm not entirely sure? I hope that's not too unhelpful.

During that time when you were so energetic and barely sleeping, did it cause serious problems—like conflicts with the other volunteers, financial issues from overspending, or anything that made people concerned enough to intervene?

Oh, goodness... well, I really didn't want to cause any trouble, but... I suppose things did get a little messy. I feel terrible even saying it, because I truly meant well with the fundraiser. 

But, um, since I started feeling so exhausted and just... unable to keep up with everything I promised, my husband has had to step in and help. Bless his heart, he's taken over most of the household chores for now. And... well, he actually had to call the historical society for me. I just felt so awful about falling behind on my commitments, and I couldn't quite face the people who were waiting on me. It's so unlike me to let people down like that. 

I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... he just helped me smooth things over a bit. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm doing this right.
How long has this current stretch of feeling exhausted, sleeping poorly, and struggling to keep up with things lasted—has it been going on for two weeks or more?

Oh, dear... well, I suppose it has been quite a while now. I really hate to admit it, because I know I should have pulled myself together by now, but... yes, it's definitely been more than two weeks. 

Actually, um... since all those orders for the fundraiser fell behind and... well, when things got a bit tense with the other volunteers... I've just been stuck in this sort of low, guilty place for... oh, goodness, it's been about nine months now. I feel so embarrassed saying that out loud. I really try to be positive and helpful, and I hate feeling like I've just been dragging my feet for so long. 

I know that sounds like an awfully long time to be in a slump... I hope you don't think poorly of me for letting it go on this long. I really am trying my best to get back to normal. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
During these past nine months, have you found yourself losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or having thoughts of death or that life isn't worth living?

Oh, goodness... well, I wouldn't say I've had any... any terrible thoughts like that. I really do try to focus on the blessings I have, you know? My husband is so good to me, and I wouldn't want to think about anything so dark. 

But as for losing interest... I suppose... well, I feel awful admitting this, because I used to just love it so much. I used to go out every morning to check on my garden, and I was always working on my own quilt entries for the local fairs. It brought me such joy. But lately... oh, I don't know what's wrong with me. I just look at the fabric piles and the new seed catalogs that come in the mail, and I just... I don't feel much of anything at all. 

It feels so ungrateful of me to say that, when I have so many nice things to work with. I really hope I'm not sounding like a complainer. I just can't seem to find that spark I used to have for them. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying my best to explain it right.

During that time when you were so full of energy and barely sleeping, did you notice yourself talking much faster than usual, having racing thoughts, feeling unusually confident or capable, or doing things that were out of character for you, like spending more money than planned?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose I might have been a bit more talkative than usual. I really didn't mean to dominate the conversation, I just... I had so many ideas, you know? 

I feel a little embarrassed thinking back on it now, but during the committee meetings, I... well, I would just get so excited talking about the quilt patterns and the budgets and all the publicity ideas. I guess I was talking awfully fast. A few of the other ladies tried to jump in and say something, and... oh, it sounds so rude of me, but I just kept going. It wasn't that I wanted to talk over them, I promise! It just felt like... like if I stopped, all those wonderful ideas would just vanish, and stopping felt almost impossible right then. 

I really hope they didn't think I was being bossy or disrespectful. I just wanted everything to be perfect for the fundraiser. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I hope I'm not making myself sound too dreadful.
During these past nine months of feeling low, have you noticed any significant change in your appetite or weight, either eating much more or much less than usual?

Oh, um... well, as for my appetite... I don't think there's been any big change, really. I always try to make sure my husband has a nice dinner, so I'm still cooking and sitting down with him. 

I suppose... well, I might not be quite as hungry as I usually am, but I really haven't lost or gained any weight that I've noticed. My clothes still fit the same, thank goodness. I know some people stop eating when they feel down, but I've been trying very hard to keep up my routines so I don't worry anyone. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have much to report on that front. I really am trying to pay attention to my health, I promise. Does that answer your question okay?

During these past nine months, how has this low mood affected your ability to concentrate, make decisions, or keep up with your usual daily responsibilities—are you still able to manage most day-to-day tasks, or has it become very difficult to function?

Oh, goodness... well, I really try my hardest to keep up with everything. I don't want to be a burden on anyone, especially my husband. He works so hard already. 

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest—and I feel just terrible admitting this—it has gotten quite difficult. I... well, I just haven't been able to keep up with my commitments like I usually do. The historical society, for instance... I'm usually so involved, but lately, I just couldn't face the people waiting on me. I felt so guilty about it, but I just couldn't bring myself to go. 

My sweet husband... he's had to step in and take over a lot of the household routines, and he even handled things with the historical society for me. I feel so ashamed that he had to do that. A wife ought to be able to manage her own home and her own responsibilities, don't you think? I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy. I'm trying so hard to get back to normal. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.

Oh, goodness... well, I really try my hardest to keep up with everything. I don't want to be a burden on anyone, especially my husband. He works so hard already. 

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest—and I feel just terrible admitting this—it has gotten quite difficult. I... well, I just haven't been able to keep up with my commitments like I usually do. The historical society, for instance... I'm usually so involved, but lately, I just couldn't face the people waiting on me. I felt so guilty about it, but I just couldn't bring myself to go. 

My sweet husband... he's had to step in and take over a lot of the household routines, and he even handled things with the historical society for me. I feel so ashamed that he had to do that. A wife ought to be able to manage her own home and her own responsibilities, don't you think? I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy. I'm trying so hard to get back to normal. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
